## Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-01 jurisdiction in a determination, sub-national codes, climate and culture

This is a resolution by an Opus-class model under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-12 ("I guess opus can do it", entry above), judged against the owner's three criteria. **It is not the owner's words**, it stands until the owner reverses it, and under the delegation's condition (d) it is **not to be relied on until a second, independent Opus-class instance has checked it**. The reasoning, the facts checked and the commands are in `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS.md` (section OD-01).

OD-01: one determination, with typed climate and cultural conditions; sub-national codes with a parent

**The resolution.** One live determination per parameter and lens set, each in-scope jurisdiction's figure shown beside it as a spread by pointer (the comparison view). Where a source conditions a figure on climate or cultural context, that is a typed condition on the figure and the determination branches by it (OR-2); a cultural caveat from another source is a pointer note, never a value. A sub-national instrument carries its own code with its country as parent. Whether a sub-national jurisdiction owes research coverage of its own is referred to the reserved decision on scope (OD-04 in the register).

**What decided it.** Criterion 1 (integrity): the determination key is ruled (2026-08-26, 2026-08-28) and a per-jurisdiction determination would change it and count adoptions as findings; filing an Ontario or Flemish instrument under its country misstates provenance. Criterion 2: one best practice with the jurisdictions beside it is what the owner asked for on 2026-10-30. Criterion 3: climate and culture are conditions some groups' provisions turn on (the 2026-04-07 thermoregulation and Kawa rules; `governance/armature_v4_resolutions.md` Q29).

**Reversal condition.** A parameter whose values cannot be compared across jurisdictions on one scale, or the owner requiring a determination per jurisdiction; for parents, a scope rule that the roll-up misroutes.

CONDITION: any session designing the jurisdiction registry, the comparison view or render, filing a sub-national instrument, or recording a climatic or cultural condition.
ACTION: (1) Keep one determination per parameter and lens set; show jurisdictions as a spread by pointer. (2) Type climate and cultural conditions on figures; never key a determination on them. (3) File a sub-national instrument under its own code with a parent; correct held rows forward in a research pull request. (4) Leave sub-national coverage to the owner's scope decision. (5) Do not rely on this entry until the independent check of condition (d) is recorded.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — delegated resolution, not an owner statement.


## Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-02 the language of a page, and how a translated quotation is shown

A resolution by an Opus-class model under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-12, judged against the owner's three criteria; **not the owner's words**; standing until the owner reverses it; **not to be relied on until the independent check of condition (d) is recorded**. Reasoning and evidence: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS.md` (section OD-02).

**The resolution.** Pages are in English for this edition. Every non-English quotation, term and clause is shown in its own language and script, with our translation beside it marked as a translation with its translator and review status; the original carries its language tag (WCAG 2.2, 3.1.2 Language of Parts). **The resolution.** Equivalence: the two name or measure the same thing and are interchangeable. **Reversal condition.** The owner glossing the words otherwise, or judged relations showing similarity and commonality cannot be told apart reliably.

## Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-25 which relations synthesis records, and who may judge them

A resolution by an Opus-class model under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-12, judged against the owner's three criteria; **not the owner's words**; standing until the owner reverses it. Reasoning and evidence: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS.md` (section OD-25).

**The resolution.** Equivalence: the two name or measure the same thing and are interchangeable. Adjacency: distinct things that bear on or constrain each other (the owner's swept-path example). A recorded relation carries its judge and warrant; candidates found by query are not recorded without judgment.

**What decided it.** Criterion 1: the four license different acts, so only equivalence and commonality may ground unification; conflict and convergence already have homes (rule 5); a relation that decides what is unified is synthesis and takes the Opus floor. Criteria 2 and 3: the discussion can say which relation it rests on, and adjacency across lenses is where compound effects appear.

**Reversal condition.** The owner glossing the words otherwise, or judged relations showing similarity and commonality cannot be told apart reliably.

CONDITION: any session recording or judging a relation between parameters, clauses, instruments, jurisdictions or figures.
ACTION: (1) Use one of the four kinds, with its test. (2) Record judge and warrant; judge at the Opus floor. (3) Unify only on equivalence or commonality. (4) Keep conflict and convergence in their own tables.

I resolved 19 of the 20 delegated decisions and referred OD-10 back whole. Four of the 19 have a part referred back. All 19 are written up and each has its ledger entry; the database is unchanged.

**What I wrote** (nothing else was touched: no task files, scripts, schemas, governance files, skills or git state; no `run_checks --all`; no agents spawned):
- `/home/user/guidebook/workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS.md`: verdict first, then one section per decision covering what I checked, the three-criteria test, the answer in the register's form, the reversal condition, what it unblocks, the implied task-file changes and a confidence level.
- `/home/user/guidebook/references/project-standards.md`: one entry appended per resolved decision. No existing line changed (`git diff references/project-standards.md | grep -c '^-[^-]'` prints 0). The D-27 loop now prints 1 for each of the 19 and 0 for OD-10 and the nine reserved decisions.
- `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` was `c9ecb8461baf2d36ba73215d991f4b46ab97b25458b6b2e3b471e9b401ab7c4d` before and after.

**Counts** (from the file: `grep -c '^\*\*Status:\*\* RESOLVED'` and `grep -c '^\*\*Status:\*\* REFERRED BACK'` on `DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS.md`): 19 resolved, 1 referred back.

**Why OD-10 went back.** The owner has given "provisional" two meanings:
- **2026-09-09 (evening):** "you have to compute it." That ruling covers the state that `assess_cell.py` computes from the evidence tiers, and the ratified definition in `governance/evidence-methodology.md` §2.3 makes provisional a strength-of-evidence state.
- **2026-10-30:** "provisional means that we have to go back and review the source again."

Each option on the register would override one of those statements, which delegation condition (e) forbids. The deciding context is the question the owner's answer 10 was replying to, and that transcript is not in the repository. The file offers the owner a reading but does not settle it.

**Parts referred back inside resolved decisions:**
- **OD-01:** whether a province or state owes research coverage of its own (that belongs to OD-04, which is reserved).
- **OD-05:** whether a study whose finding doesn't depend on its country counts as "evidence from a jurisdiction" under the 2026-09-28 standing order.
- **OD-14:** the wording for part-time wheelchair users.
- **OD-22:** every open owner prompt other than OR-10b. OR-5b, OR-6c, OR-22b and OR-23b touch evidence-tier definitions; OT-2 is a term definition the owner approves himself; I didn't take on OR-14b or OR-25. OW-1b and OW-1c are answered by OD-12. OR-1c and OR-17b were already answered by the owner on 2026-11-06.

**Confidence:**
- **Medium:** OD-03, OD-12, OD-14, OD-22, OD-24 (the starting list of quantity kinds; the parameter-granularity rule itself is high), OD-25 and OD-30.
- **Low:** only the line between "similarity" and "commonality" in OD-25. The owner gave the four words without defining them, so my definitions are a reading.

**Where I disagreed with the audit's recommendation:**
- **OD-29:** both a connection and an admission edge are retired in place. The audit chose to let the admission edge be deleted, but the 2026-09-16 ruling covers all data rows and reserves exceptions to the owner. `unlink_admission` also stores the removed edge as a note appended inside another cell, which the owner's 2026-11-06 rule against joined cells forbids.
- **OD-14:** every row is judged by the users it names; only rows that name no one more specific than mobility are copied to both new codes.
- **OD-18:** I confirmed the stage conditions with five corrections rather than as listed.
- **OD-25:** I kept the owner's four relation kinds and left conflict and convergence in the tables they already have.
- **OD-03:** I chose a combination of options rather than option (a) alone.

**The four that need the independent check:**
- **OD-01 (low to moderate).** One determination per parameter and disability lens, with each jurisdiction's figure shown beside it, is close to forced: the owner ruled the determination's key twice (2026-08-26 and 2026-08-28) and asked for a comparison table. Typed climate and cultural conditions follow existing project rules. The part most open to challenge is giving provinces and regions their own codes under a parent country. The facts behind it are firm: the Ontario code is stored as `CA` and a Flemish decree as `BE`.
- **OD-02 (moderate).** Pages in English with the original shown beside every translation. Criterion 2 (legibility) would favour pages in several languages for readers in Japan, Korea, China and elsewhere. That loses only under the unratified assumption that criterion 1 (integrity) comes first. A reviewer who weights legibility more could reasonably disagree.
- **OD-12 (moderate to high, the most contestable).** I chose templates and a render table rebuilt in full at each build. I moved any model-written discussion out of render and into synthesis rows, where only Opus-class models write. That is my reconciliation of the owner's OW-1 request for "complete prose" in a render table with his 2026-10-30 instruction to present information without claiming it is correct. A reviewer could read OW-1 as wanting the prose written and stored.
- **OD-14 (moderate).** I depart from the literal fan-out ruling of 2026-08-25. My argument is that the reason given for it (no judging before synthesis) was removed when the owner overruled DR-2026-08-24 §2.4 on 2026-08-27, and that the link table from OR-1c means tagging both codes no longer copies the figure. The ruling's "never fan out a grade" is kept in full. A reviewer could hold that the fan-out still binds.

**Gaps the resolutions expose:**
- No task gives `search_admissions` a retired mark or turns `unlink-admission` into a retire verb. OD-29 needs a new tooling task.
- OD-11 (the gap register spans stages) could silently remove the three research-stage paths that `walkability.py` currently routes through `gaps`. The task that edits the stage map must run the instrument before and after.
- `evidence_sources.pub_title_en`, `translation_method` and `translation_reviewed` are an unused second home for translations, which T-049 should absorb or point at.
- T-020 assumes a fixed list of quantity kinds in a schema check; OD-24 holds them as rows instead, so new kinds can be added as data.

**What I could not verify:**
- The context of the owner's answer 10 of 2026-10-30 (OD-10).
- Whether `walkability.py` counts a cross-stage table as a member of a stage. I inferred it from the output header, not the code.
- The full set of code that reads `search_admissions`; I named only the known readers.
- `sessions/` was searched with `git grep`, not read end to end.

For the record, I ran `walkability.py` once, read-only; the database hash didn't change.

31	- **Climate and culture as conditions.** PS:370-373 (hot-humid thermoregulation), PS:378 (ISO wayfinding "without cultural or climate adaptation"), PS:381 and PS:407-411 (PAS 6463 and Kawa), `governance/armature_v4_resolutions.md` Q29 (lines 627-644). Neither supports *branching* a determination by culture; they support a flag and a note. The resolution's branching rests on OR-2 (PS:4616, "Branches, and an empty headline when all are conditioned"), whose prompt (`governance/owner-browser.yaml`, OR-2) is about any conditional claim. So the branch is warranted by OR-2, not by the Kawa rule, and the Kawa rule's Person Mode flag must survive it. Q29 is an Opus 4.6 resolution ("Author: Opus 4.6", file header), not an owner ruling.

56	## OD-02 — The language of a page; how a translated quotation is shown
57	
58	### A. Fact check
59	
60	- **No ruling sets a page language.** `git grep -n -i -E "page language|language of (the|a) page|pages in english|written in english" -- governance references/project-standards.md decisions sessions` finds nothing on point. **Verified.**
61	- **But an owner statement bears on it directly and is not cited.** PS:5222, the first owner statement of 2026-11-12: "ensure that our pipeline can be run in all directions at any stage in such a manner where we can dynamically research, adjudicate, synthesize, specify and **render across a multitude of languages** and jurisdictions." Its ledger entry records "What 'render across languages' means … [is] open and [an] `OWNER DECISION REQUIRED` item" (PS:5236), and its ACTION (1) is "Treat the three objective statements as live requirements on the pipeline" (PS:5239). The resolutions file and the ledger entry for OD-02 do not mention it.
62	- **Ninth statement (PS:5358):** "probably at synthesis or whatever we need to actually translate everything". Quoted correctly; the resolution's use (quotations may be translated) matches the register's narrowing (REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN, OD-02).
63	- **Eighth statement of 2026-11-06 (PS:5200-5215).** The owner's words are "you obviously can have English words for these rows." and "we are trying to avoid english BIAS". The resolutions file quotes the recording session's gloss (PS:5209: "English must not be the pivot that decides which concepts exist, what the standard form is, or how a non-English concept is described") and then, in the criteria test and in the ledger entry, narrows it to "which concepts exist and which column is read first". The narrowing drops "how a non-English concept is described", which is exactly what an English translation beside a quotation does. The quoted sentence is the recorder's reading, not the owner's verbatim, but the owner's own words ("avoid english BIAS") are wider still, not narrower.
64	- **WCAG 2.2 SC 3.1.2 Language of Parts** is Level AA, inside the owner's WCAG 2.2 AA requirement (PS:4847, 4858). **Verified.**
65	- `governance/audience-priority.md` names four audiences and no language (the resolver says so). The resolver's statement that the audiences "include readers in JP, KR, CN, DE, FR" is an inference from P1+P2+P3 scope, not a recorded audience.
66	
67	### B. Authority check
68	
69	- The resolution does not override a ruling: no ruling fixes a page language, and keeping the page language a render parameter leaves "render across a multitude of languages" reachable.
70	- It does, however, settle in practice a reading of the owner's own words (PS:5222) that the ledger reserved as an owner question (PS:5236). Under the delegation that is allowed only as a reading under condition (c) ("a defensible reading and not a statement of what the owner meant"). The resolution is not labelled as one, and does not name the statement it reads.
71	- The anti-English-bias rulings: English pages with the original shown first or beside, language-tagged, is a defensible way to avoid bias on the reading surface. The ledger sentence that claims those rulings do not reach the reading surface at all overstates; it should claim only that this design meets them.
72	
73	### C. Criteria check
74	
75	The C1-over-C2 call rests on the unratified priority assumption, as the resolver says. One argument against option (ii) is overstated: "every fixed sentence of every page would then be unreviewed translated prose of our own". Under the resolver's own OD-12, fixed sentences are a bounded set of templates, translatable once per language, and under its own OD-30 a translation can be reviewed by a second Opus-class instance before a reader sees it. So (ii), or a hybrid (English plus one further page language), is cheaper and less C1-hostile than portrayed. A reader who weights C2 or C3 more, or who reads PS:5222 as requiring pages in several languages, would reach a hybrid. Contestability: moderate. The stated confidence ("medium on English as the only page language") is honest.
76	
77	### D. Consequence check
78	
79	Releases T-037 (render) and T-112 (target language English). Nothing is published yet (pre-launch), and translations are additive rows attached by pointer, so reversal is cheap. One risk the resolution creates: a "page language parameter" with a single value and no test that exercises a second value is a hard-coded behaviour in effect (seventh statement of 2026-11-12, PS:5322: "pipeline must not have hard coded behaviours"). A second risk: T-112's English translations become the medium through which synthesis compares non-English evidence ("so that it can be compared and discussed together", PS:5360). That makes English the comparison pivot at synthesis, a stage choice the ninth statement left open. OD-02 should bind the page only.

81	### Verdict: CONFIRMED WITH CORRECTIONS
82

Ledger entry and resolutions file: add that this is **a reading of the owner's statement of 2026-11-12 (PS:5222, "render across a multitude of languages") under condition (c)**, namely that rendering across languages is met by showing each source's own language, tagged, beside our translation, with the page language a parameter, and not by pages in several languages in this edition. Name PS:5236 as the place the question was reserved.

85	3. ACTION (3) gains a test: the renderer must emit a page in a second language by data alone (a template set and a page-language value), with no code edit, so the parameter is not dead (seventh statement).
86	4. Scope the English target to display: "T-112's target language is English for display; this resolution does not fix the language in which synthesis compares evidence."
87	5. Resolutions file C2 bullet: remove or correct "every fixed sentence of every page would then be unreviewed translated prose of our own" in the light of OD-12 (bounded templates) and OD-30 (review before display).

103	
104	- **OW-1 "complete prose" is reconciled, not sidestepped:** the render table holds complete prose, and the judged parts come from synthesis rows. That matches OW-1's "rendering … on the basis of whatever specification has been synthesized" and OR-6's "with a synthesis approach".

126	## OD-14 — Carrying the rows written under `MOB` since the split was ratified
127	
128	### A. Fact check
129	
130	- **The ruling (PS:1291-1313).** The owner's words are only: *"yes, AMB and WHEEL to fan out."* The operative scope is "All **31** `item_population_links` rows keyed `MOB` … become **62** rows". The reason ("It is the anti-erasure choice: the alternative — resolving each of the 31 by hand now — would decide applicability by inference, before synthesis, which is what `DR-2026-08-24` §2.4 forbids") is the recording session's text, not the owner's.
131	- **What the owner was actually asked.** The design the ruling "settles" (`scratchpad/session_2026-08-25-pipeline-smoke-test-mobility/logs/F5-population-split-design.md` §8 item 2): "**Fan-out vs delete for the 31 item links** … Recommended: fan out (conservation precedent). The strict §2.4 alternative — delete all 31 as pre-synthesis presupposition … One-word decision: 'fan' or 'drop'." The alternative put to the owner was *drop*, not *judge*. The design's reason for fan-out (§2.1) is anti-erasure and conservation: "assigning each row to only one member is a per-item judgment nobody has made; making it silently would erase one community from each item". It also notes that the 31 rows had `rationale_ref=NULL` and came from "the retired `applicable_groups` CSV": scaffold, not evidence.
132	- **The overruling (PS:2000-2003),** owner 2026-08-27: "overrule Aug 24 DR. we go evidence>judgment>synthesis." Its ACTION (1) supersedes "*applicability is an OUTPUT of synthesis*" and "*zero `item_population_links` is the correct pre-synthesis state*", and places the crossing at judgment. It does not mention the mobility split or its fan-out. **Verified as quoted;** the resolver's reading that it removed §2.4 is right; its reading that it thereby removed *the owner's* reason for fan-out is not, because the owner gave none, and the reason the design gave (anti-erasure) is untouched.
133	- **Grade clause.** "Not fanned out, ever: `evidence_population_match.study_population` … A grade is a fact about a paper. (Moot in practice — measured **0** MOB rows there — but recorded because the next split will not be moot.)" The design's §2.3 adds the forward rule: "Had a MOB grade existed it would be resolved by **re-grading per member against the study population** … Fan-out is never permitted in this table." OD-14's grade handling matches this. **Verified.** Grades against `MOB` now exist: `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute(\"select match_grade,count(*) from evidence_population_match where target_population='MOB' group by 1\").fetchall())"`.

The ruling's words are "not a judgement that every demand applies equally to both".
135	- **When the rows were written.** `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute(\"select min(created_at),max(created_at),count(*) from source_value_extractions where identity_code='MOB'\").fetchall())"`: every `MOB` figure postdates both the split and the 2026-08-27 overruling. They are extraction rows with quotes, not CSV scaffold. This is the strongest fact for the resolution, and the ledger entry does not use it.
136	- **OR-1c link table (PS:4926):** "link table unless that is more prone to errors". **Verified.** The table does not exist yet (T-018): `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print([r[0] for r in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table' and name like '%link%'\")])"`.
137	- **Registry state.** `select identity_code,status from base_taxonomy_identity where identity_code in ('MOB','AMB','WHEEL')` returns only `MOB`, `active`; the status vocabulary is `active`/`deprecated` (its CHECK), so "retired in place" means `deprecated`. `evidence_population_match` has no retirement column (`PRAGMA table_info(evidence_population_match)`), so "the old grade rows are retired in place" needs a schema change the resolution does not name.
138	- **Not cited, and supporting judging for provisions:** owner 2026-11-06 (second), item 2 at PS:4935 and ACTION (2) at PS:4941: "Do not tag a provision from an accessibility code ALL because its sentence names no group; leave the tag to the lens fill", and the recorded reading "Which group a provision carries is judgment's output, filled with the link table".
139	
140	### B. Authority check
141	
142	1. **The decisive argument is an implied retirement of an owner ruling.** The ledger's "What decided it" rests on: the ruling chose fan-out because judging would infer applicability before synthesis; §2.4 was overruled; so the ruling's reason is gone. Three defects. (i) The reason is the recorder's gloss, and it misstates the choice the owner made (fan or *drop*). (ii) The reason the design actually gave, anti-erasure, survives the overruling intact. (iii) Even if the reason had lapsed, a delegate concluding that an owner rule no longer binds because a later ruling removed its basis, where the later ruling does not name it, is the act the delegation reserved. OD-13 is reserved for exactly this ("Only the owner retires an owner rule where the later ruling does not name it", REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN OD-13), and condition (e) forbids a delegated resolution to override a standing ruling. **As written, this is a case that must be referred back.**
143	2. **A sound ground exists and is under-used.** The ruling's operative words are scoped to 31 `item_population_links` rows (a table since dropped); its only forward-looking clause concerns grades, and OD-14 keeps it; the rows now at issue are post-ruling extraction rows that the ruling never addressed. On that ground OD-14 decides a question the ruling left open, honours its surviving principle (anti-erasure, by fanning out rows that name neither group), and does not override it. The resolutions file mentions this ground in one clause ("it governed the 31 item links (a table since dropped)"); the ledger entry omits it and leads with the defective argument.
144	3. **Collision with an open owner question.** GAP-076 (`select status, description from gaps where gap_id='GAP-076'`): "WHICH LENS DOES A CLAUSE CARRY WHEN ITS OWN TEXT NAMES NO ONE BUT SITS UNDER A DISABILITY HEADING (MOB OR ALL) … OWNER DECISION". The 2026-11-06 (second) entry (PS:4935) leaves "one question" standing: "confirm the reading", which is "not a final ruling on MOB against ALL for a clause under a disability heading". OD-14's bucket "a row that names no one more specific than mobility is fanned out to both" includes rows whose `MOB` tag rests on a heading, not on the text. Fanning those to `AMB` and `WHEEL` presupposes the owner's answer to GAP-076 (MOB, not ALL). GAP-076 is not among the delegated twenty: `grep -n -E "GAP-076" workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` prints nothing.
145	4. The part-time wheelchair wording is correctly referred back.
146	
147	### C. Criteria check
148	
149	C1 is applied fairly to judging over blanket fan-out (supported further by the 2026-07-23 umbrella test: `AX-AMB` and `AX-WHM` demands "are **opposed**" on ramp gradient, PS:1128). C3 is applied fairly to unnamed rows. The audit's option (c) is described accurately, and its weakness is real (a provision that names wheelchair users would still be fanned to ambulant people). Option (b) is slightly strawmanned: "rows that name nobody lose their identity tag" is the audit's own consequence line, but (b) could equally leave them `MOB` pending, which the resolver does not consider. A reader weighting C3 more would prefer (a) for every non-study row, as the anti-erasure default, until judgment re-derives each. The decision turns on how much one trusts a judgment made from stored claim text (the 2026-08-27 ruling places the deep read at judgment, "with the source in hand", PS:2003-2016) as against a flagged carry. Contestability: high. "Medium" confidence is honest about the substance and not about the authority question, which the resolver did not flag at all.
150	
151	### D. Consequence check
152	
153	Releases T-102 and through it T-110 (the first determinations). T-102 is a research task that writes append-only data migrations: new `AMB`/`WHEEL` registry rows, tag links, re-graded population matches, `MOB` deprecated, a determination gate re-raised (`select gate_id, parameter_id, resolved_at from determination_gates where identity_code='MOB'`). Undoing any of it takes compensating migrations. T-110 then writes determinations keyed on the new tags, which are the first candidates for a published sentence. Retiring grade rows needs a schema change in a tooling PR first (rule 10). T-102's gate (`grep -n -F "OD-14:"`) already matches the delegated line, while its own text demands the owner's words: the gate and the delegation disagree, and the mechanical half opens.
154	
155	### Verdict: REFER BACK (as written)
156	
157	What the owner should be asked, in one line: "The 2026-08-25 fan-out ruling covered the 31 item links. For the post-split `MOB` figures and grades, may judgment tag each row by the users it names, fanning out (flagged) only rows that name neither group, and is a clause that names no one but sits under a disability heading `MOB` or `ALL` (GAP-076)?"
158	
159	If the owner prefers the delegation to carry it, the resolution must be re-issued, and checked again under condition (d), with these changes:
160	1. Ledger "What decided it": delete the argument that the ruling's reason was removed. Ground the resolution on scope: the ruling's operative words cover the 31 `item_population_links` rows; the rows at issue were written after it and after the 2026-08-27 ruling placed the crossing at judgment; its grade clause is kept in full; its surviving principle, anti-erasure, is kept by fanning out unnamed rows. Cite the 2026-11-06 (second) ACTION (2) (PS:4941).
161	2. Carve out GAP-076: rows whose `MOB` tag rests on a heading and whose text names no group are neither judged nor fanned until the owner answers GAP-076. Until then they stay `MOB`, and their count is given by command.
162	3. Resolutions file C1 bullet: correct the misattribution ("provisionally wrong for one of the two groups" is the register's wording, not the ruling's).
163	4. Name the schema change "retired in place" requires for `evidence_population_match`, as a tooling PR before T-102 (rule 10).
164	5. T-102's gate: state in the ledger entry (and implied task change) that the task waits for the recorded condition-(d) check, since `grep -F "OD-14:"` alone already matches.
165	
166	---
167	
168	## Not examined
169	
170	- The handshake ledger's HS-1 C-02, C-03 and HS-A12, and REQ-104, which the register cites as evidence for OD-01 and OD-02 (`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/01-handshake-ledger.md`). I read only line 170 (P-01-1).
171	- The scratch files of the resolving session and of the 2026-11-12 audit (`scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/`), including `audit/hs-improvement-programme.md`, IMP-20 and the AT tests, as instructed.
172	- The other sixteen delegated resolutions, except where one is named above (OD-13 by analogy; OD-30 and OD-07 as they bear on OD-02 and OD-12; OD-19 as it holds T-032).
173	- The owner's session transcripts behind the 2026-08-25 and 2026-10-29/30 answers. I relied on the ledger's verbatim quotations and on the F5 design file as the record of what was put to the owner on 2026-08-25. That the owner saw the F5 §8 framing ("fan" or "drop") and not the ledger's later wording is inferred from the ledger's "Settles the two questions the split design … put to the owner", not read from the transcript.
174	- How many `MOB` figures name a group in their text, or rest on a heading only. That needs a read of each `claim_text` and is judgment work, not a review.
175	- Whether `governance/armature_v4_resolutions.md` Q29 was ever owner-ratified; its header calls it "Authoritative resolution" by Opus 4.6, and I found no ratification line.
176	- No check suite was run; none reads these documents for meaning.

230 scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/build_batches.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Derive the remediation plan's dependency batches from the task files. Reads only; writes REMEDIATION-PLAN.md.

    python3 -I scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/build_batches.py

Nothing here is typed in: ids, titles, kinds, executors, owner decisions and hard dependencies come from each
task file's own text (section 1 table; section 2 bullets 'Tasks that must be merged' and 'Owner decisions').
A dependency written 'none (after T-nnn if both are open ...)' is SOFT: an ordering hint, not a gate.
Batch = 1 + the longest chain of hard dependencies. Within a batch, tasks that touch the same file are one
SERIAL LANE (merge in the lane's order); different lanes may be worked in parallel.
"""
import re, subprocess, datetime, collections
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/home/user/guidebook")
W = ROOT / "workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline"
OUT = W / "REMEDIATION-PLAN.md"
TASKS = sorted((W / "tasks").glob("T-[0-9]*-*.md"))


def section(text, n):
    m = re.search(rf"^## {n}\. .*?$(.*?)(?=^## \d+\. |\Z)", text, re.S | re.M)
    return m.group(1) if m else ""


def cell(text, label):
    m = re.search(rf"^\| {label} \| (.*?) \|\s*$", text, re.M)
    return m.group(1).strip() if m else ""


def bullet(sec2, label):
    m = re.search(rf"^- \*\*{label}[^*]*\*\*(.*?)(?=^- \*\*|\Z)", sec2, re.S | re.M)
    return m.group(1).strip() if m else ""


tasks = {}
for f in TASKS:
    t = f.read_text()
    tid = re.match(r"# (T-\d+)", t).group(1)
    title = re.sub(r"^# T-\d+\s+", "", t.splitlines()[0]).strip()
    s2, s4 = section(t, 2), section(t, 4)
    dep_txt = bullet(s2, "Tasks that must be merged")
    dep_txt = dep_txt.split("Check by running")[0]
    soft = set()
    if dep_txt.lower().lstrip().startswith("none ("):
        soft = set(re.findall(r"T-\d+", dep_txt))
        hard = set()
    elif dep_txt.lower().lstrip().startswith("none"):
        hard = set()
    else:
        hard = set(re.findall(r"T-\d+", dep_txt))
    hard.discard(tid)
    od_txt = bullet(s2, "Owner decisions")
    ods = set() if od_txt.lower().startswith("none") else set(re.findall(r"OD-\d+", od_txt))
    paths = sorted(set(re.findall(r"`((?:scripts|schemas|governance|skills|\.claude|\.github)/[A-Za-z0-9_./\-]+\.[a-z]+)`", s4)))
    paths = [p for p in paths if "/migrations/" not in p]
    if "RESEARCH" in cell(t, "Kind"):
        paths = []  # a research task writes rows through the sanctioned path; the tools it calls are not files it edits
    tasks[tid] = dict(
        id=tid, file=f.name, title=title, wave=cell(t, "Wave"), kind="RESEARCH" if "RESEARCH" in cell(t, "Kind") else "TOOLING",
        sonnet="NOT FOR SONNET" not in cell(t, "Executor"), hard=hard, soft=soft, ods=ods, paths=paths,
        piloted=bool(re.search(r"\*\*Pilot status\.\*\* \*\*Piloted", t)))

# --- batches: longest chain of hard dependencies
memo, stack = {}, set()


def depth(t):
    if t in memo:
        return memo[t]
    if t in stack:
        raise SystemExit(f"CYCLE through {t}")
    stack.add(t)
    d = 1 + max([depth(x) for x in tasks[t]["hard"] if x in tasks] or [0])
    stack.discard(t)
    memo[t] = d
    return d


missing = sorted({d for t in tasks.values() for d in t["hard"] if d not in tasks})
for t in tasks:
    tasks[t]["batch"] = depth(t)
nb = max(t["batch"] for t in tasks.values())

# --- status
def status(t):
    if not t["sonnet"]:
        return "NOT FOR SONNET"
    if t["ods"]:
        return "OWNER: " + ",".join(sorted(t["ods"], key=lambda x: int(x[3:])))
    return "READY"


# a task is 'reachable by Sonnet' if it and every hard ancestor is READY
def anc(t, seen=None):
    seen = seen if seen is not None else set()
    for d in tasks[t]["hard"]:
        if d in tasks and d not in seen:
            seen.add(d)
            anc(d, seen)
    return seen


for tid, t in tasks.items():
    t["status"] = status(t)
    blockers = [a for a in anc(tid) if status(tasks[a]) != "READY"]
    t["reach"] = "yes" if t["status"] == "READY" and not blockers else ("after " + ", ".join(sorted(blockers, key=lambda x: int(x[2:]))) if t["status"] == "READY" else "no")

# --- serial lanes inside a batch: connected components over shared paths and soft deps
def lanes(ids):
    parent = {i: i for i in ids}

    def find(x):
        while parent[x] != x:
            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
            x = parent[x]
        return x

    def union(a, b):
        parent[find(a)] = find(b)

    for a in ids:
        for b in ids:
            if a < b and (set(tasks[a]["paths"]) & set(tasks[b]["paths"]) or b in tasks[a]["soft"] or a in tasks[b]["soft"]):
                union(a, b)
    comp = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for i in ids:
        comp[find(i)].append(i)
    key = lambda i: (tasks[i]["kind"] == "RESEARCH", int(i[2:]))
    return sorted((sorted(v, key=key) for v in comp.values()), key=lambda v: key(v[0]))


# --- owner-decision queue
od_blocks = collections.defaultdict(list)
for tid, t in tasks.items():
    for o in t["ods"]:
        od_blocks[o].append(tid)

# --- critical path (longest hard chain)
def chain(t):
    best = []
    for d in tasks[t]["hard"]:
        if d in tasks:
            c = chain(d)
            if len(c) > len(best):
                best = c
    return best + [t]


crit = max((chain(t) for t in tasks), key=len)

sha = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC")
L = []
A = L.append
A("# Remediation plan, in batches by dependency\n")
A(f"_Generated {now} from the {len(tasks)} task files at commit {sha} by `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/build_batches.py`. "
  "Nothing below is typed in: re-run the generator (`python3 -I scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/build_batches.py`) after any task file changes, and trust the generator over this text (CLAUDE.md rule 7a)._\n")
A("**What this is.** The entry document for a Sonnet executor. `REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` is the index (why, owner decision register, Definition of Done); `tasks/T-<id>-*.md` is the one self-contained file per task; this file says **in what order, in what groups, and where to stop.** "
  "Evidence base: `01-handshake-ledger.md` and the audit in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/`.\n")
A("## 1. How to execute\n")
A("1. **Merge this workplan first.** Every task file sets `$BASE` to `origin/main` once the workplan is on it, and to the workplan branch before that.")
A("2. **Take one batch at a time, in order.** A batch is the set of tasks whose hard dependencies all lie in earlier batches. Do not start batch *n* until every READY task of batch *n-1* is merged and its after-test is green on `$BASE`.")
A("3. **Inside a batch, work lanes in parallel and tasks in a lane serially.** A lane is a set of tasks that touch the same file (or that a task file says to sequence). Merge a lane's tasks in the order listed; where `REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` gives its own merge order for some of them (Wave 0), that order wins, because it also accounts for the characterisation harness of T-014 which must exist before the changes it compares.")
A("4. **One task, one pull request, one executor, one task file.** Run the task's red test before, the same test after, the gate once (`scripts/preflight.sh --base \"$BASE\" --explain`), and the adversarial pass once before opening the pull request. Rule 9: open the pull request last, then unsubscribe.")
A("5. **Stop at a status that is not READY.** `OWNER: OD-nn` means the owner's answer (in the form the register gives) must be in `references/project-standards.md` first. `NOT FOR SONNET` means an Opus-class session or the Fable agent does it. Neither is an invitation to improvise.")
A("6. **Tooling merges before the research it unlocks (rule 10).** A research task never shares a pull request with tooling, and its row writes go only through the write path of CLAUDE.md §4.")
A("7. **The first execution of an unpiloted task is its pilot.** List any defect found in its task file in the pull request.\n")
A("## 2. The batches at a glance\n")
A("| Batch | Tasks | READY | OWNER-blocked | NOT FOR SONNET | Tooling / research | Lanes |")
A("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
for b in range(1, nb + 1):
    ids = [t for t in tasks if tasks[t]["batch"] == b]
    c = collections.Counter(tasks[t]["status"].split(":")[0] for t in ids)
    A(f"| {b} | {len(ids)} | {c['READY']} | {c['OWNER']} | {c['NOT FOR SONNET']} | {sum(tasks[t]['kind']=='TOOLING' for t in ids)} / {sum(tasks[t]['kind']=='RESEARCH' for t in ids)} | {len(lanes(ids))} |")
A("\nCounts are derived; the commands that check them: `ls workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-[0-9]*-*.md | wc -l`, and the generator's own output.\n")
A(f"**Longest dependency chain ({len(crit)} tasks):** " + " → ".join(f"{t} ({tasks[t]['status']})" for t in crit) + ".\n")
if missing:
    A(f"**Dependencies naming a task with no file (fix the task file):** {', '.join(missing)}\n")

for b in range(1, nb + 1):
    ids = [t for t in tasks if tasks[t]["batch"] == b]
    A(f"## Batch {b}\n")
    if b == 1:
        A("**Entry:** the workplan is on the integration base. No task is a prerequisite.\n")
    else:
        prev = sorted({d for t in ids for d in tasks[t]["hard"]}, key=lambda x: int(x[2:]))
        A("**Entry:** merged and green on `$BASE`: " + ", ".join(prev) + ".\n")
    A("| Task | Title | Wave | Kind | Status | Reachable by Sonnet now | Hard deps | Pilot |")
    A("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for t in sorted(ids, key=lambda x: int(x[2:])):
        x = tasks[t]
        A(f"| [{t}](tasks/{x['file']}) | {x['title'][:90]} | {x['wave']} | {x['kind']} | {x['status']} | {x['reach']} | {', '.join(sorted(x['hard'], key=lambda y: int(y[2:]))) or '—'} | {'piloted' if x['piloted'] else 'not piloted'} |")
    A("\n**Lanes** (parallel across, serial within; the shared file is the reason):\n")
    for i, lane in enumerate(lanes(ids), 1):
        shared = sorted(set.intersection(*[set(tasks[t]["paths"]) for t in lane])) if len(lane) > 1 else []
        why = f" — share `{shared[0]}`" if shared else (" — sequenced by a soft dependency or a chain of shared files" if len(lane) > 1 else "")
        A(f"- Lane {b}.{i}: " + " → ".join(lane) + why)
    nfs = sorted((t for t in ids if not tasks[t]["sonnet"]), key=lambda x: int(x[2:]))
    own = sorted((t for t in ids if tasks[t]["sonnet"] and tasks[t]["ods"]), key=lambda x: int(x[2:]))
    stops = []
    if nfs:
        stops.append("not for Sonnet: " + ", ".join(nfs))
    if own:
        stops.append("waiting on the owner: " + ", ".join(f"{t} ({'/'.join(sorted(tasks[t]['ods']))})" for t in own))
    A("\n**Exit:** every READY task above is merged and its section 6 after-test is green on `$BASE`; `scripts/preflight.sh --base \"$BASE\" --explain` is green on `$BASE`." +
      (f" **Stops in this batch:** {'; '.join(stops)}." if stops else "") + "\n")

A("## Owner decision queue (what each answer releases)\n")
A("Answer forms and options are in the register in `REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` (grep `^### OD-`). An answer binds only once the ledger quotes it (`references/project-standards.md`).\n")
A("| Decision | Releases | In batches |")
A("|---|---|---|")
for o in sorted(od_blocks, key=lambda x: int(x[3:])):
    A(f"| {o} | {', '.join(sorted(od_blocks[o], key=lambda x: int(x[2:])))} | {', '.join(str(b) for b in sorted({tasks[t]['batch'] for t in od_blocks[o]}))} |")
inreg = set(re.findall(r"^### (OD-\d+)", (W / "REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md").read_text(), re.M))
A(f"\nDecisions in the register that no task file lists as a precondition: {', '.join(sorted(inreg - set(od_blocks), key=lambda x: int(x[3:]))) or 'none'}.\n")
A("## NOT FOR SONNET\n")
A("| Task | Title | Batch | Owner decisions |")
A("|---|---|---|---|")
for t in sorted((t for t in tasks if not tasks[t]["sonnet"]), key=lambda x: int(x[2:])):
    x = tasks[t]
    A(f"| [{t}](tasks/{x['file']}) | {x['title'][:80]} | {x['batch']} | {', '.join(sorted(x['ods'])) or '—'} |")
A("\nEach file says who does it. Everything that depends on one of these waits for it (the 'Reachable by Sonnet now' column names the blockers).\n")
A("## Where the pilots stand\n")
A("`grep -L \"Not piloted\" workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-*.md` lists the tasks a pilot has touched. Results, defects found and what changed in the plan are in section 12 of `REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` and in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/pilot/`.\n")
OUT.write_text("\n".join(L))
print("tasks", len(tasks), "batches", nb, "missing deps", missing, "crit", len(crit))
for b in range(1, nb + 1):
    ids = [t for t in tasks if tasks[t]["batch"] == b]
    print(b, len(ids), collections.Counter(tasks[t]["status"].split(":")[0] for t in ids))

# T-024  Jurisdictions in a table the writers read

_One task, one pull request. Read `CLAUDE.md` first; beyond it this file is self-contained. Index, order and the owner decision register: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`. Evidence base: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/01-handshake-ledger.md`, as corrected by `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/fa-corrections-for-suite.md` (where they differ, the corrections govern). Every number in this file was read on 2026-11-12 and is given with the command that produces it: re-run the command; do not trust the number._

**Pilot status.** Not piloted. Three tasks of this plan were executed in scratch clones (T-006, T-008, T-010) and the defects they showed in the task files were corrected in every file by one generator; this file's own steps have not been executed by anyone. Its evidence command was run on 2026-11-12 and printed what section 3 states. Expect to find a defect in this file, and report it rather than work around it.

## 1. Identity

| | |
|---|---|
| Task | T-024 |
| Title | Jurisdictions in a table the writers read |
| Wave | 3 |
| Layer (CLAUDE.md §3) | 1 |
| Kind | **TOOLING** (CLAUDE.md rule 10: tooling and research never share a pull request) |
| Executor | Sonnet-class |
| Traces to | IMP-17 in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/hs-improvement-programme.md` |

## 2. Preconditions

## 4. The change
1. **One table, `translations`, by schema migration.** A translation points at the cell it translates and never replaces or copies it. Columns: `translation_id` (integer key); the pointer `source_table`, `source_column`, `source_row_key` (the row's primary-key value as text); `source_sha256` (the hash of the cell's text when it was translated, so a later change to the original is seen; a hash is not a copy); `target_language`; `translated_text` (NULL only while requested); `status` with a CHECK (`requested`, `translated`, `reviewed`, `rejected`); `translator_kind` with a CHECK (`model`, `tool`, `person`) and `translator_name` (the model id, the tool and version, or the person), both required once `status` is past `requested`; `requested_at_stage` (the stage that asked); `due_stage` (NULL means the rule of item 4 decides; a value is an explicit override for this row); `reviewed_by_kind`, `reviewed_by_name`, `reviewed_at`, required exactly when `status` is `reviewed` or `rejected`; `superseded_by_translation_id` (a corrected translation is a new row; the old one is retired in place); and the four session and time columns every table carries. CHECKs hold those consistency rules. There is no column that says "this is a translation": the table is the mark, and a flag that is always true informs nobody.
2. **One view, `v_translations_current`:** rows that are `translated` or `reviewed` and not superseded. It is the only read surface. It never names `translated_text` as if it were a source column, and nothing joins it into a view under the name of the column it translates.
3. **Three verbs in `scripts/db.py`,** each refusing what it should. `request-translation` (pointer, `--target-language`, `--stage`): validates the pointer against the live schema (the table and column exist, by `sqlite_master` and `PRAGMA table_info`; the row exists by its primary key; the cell is text and not empty). It reads the cell itself and stores the hash; it never accepts the original retyped. It refuses a target language `lang_jur_map` does not hold, using the function `log-search` uses (`grep -n 'not a language lang_jur_map holds' scripts/db.py`), and a target equal to the source's recorded language where the pointed row leads to one. `record-translation` (a request id, or a pointer to create and fill in one call; `--text`, `--translator-kind`, `--translator-name`): applies the fidelity rule of item 5. `review-translation` (`--verdict reviewed|rejected`, the reviewer's kind and name, a reason on rejection). No list of translatable tables is typed anywhere: any text cell of any table can be pointed at. `--stage` is validated against the stage ids of `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml`.
4. **The default stage is a rule held once, not a literal in code.** `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml` gains one top-level key, `translation:` with `default_stage: synthesis` (the owner: "we can set a rule for synthesis to translate, which isn't hardcoding necessarily"). `schemas/pipeline_contract.py` gains the matching optional field and validates that the value is one of the contract's own stage ids. The verbs read it through one function: a request made without `--due-stage` falls due at the rule's stage, computed when it is read, never stored; one read-only verb, `translations --due-at <stage>`, lists what is due there. No stage name appears in the verbs' code. The target language has no default until OD-02 is answered: `--target-language` is required.
5. **Fidelity, checked at `record-translation`.** The original is kept by construction (it is never touched). The numbers must agree: with the number reader of T-008, every number the original cell states as a numeral must be stated in the translation, and every number the translation states must be stated in the original or, where the pointed cell is the `claim_text` of a figure, be a number of that row's verified `claimed_value` (this covers a number the source writes in words). A translation that adds, drops or changes a figure is refused. A translation of a cell whose hash no longer matches is refused: request it again.
6. **What this is not.** The aliases typed `TRANSLATION` in `term_aliases` are search forms generated in other languages; they stay where they are, flagged as search aids (T-026 types their attestation), and are neither moved here nor deleted. A translation row never becomes an alias or a term: a concept is minted only from an observed phrase, as now (no back-translation). A translation of an attested non-English form is an aid to discussion that points at the alias row. `value_as_written` on a figure (T-008) is the same idea at the grain of one cell: the source's wording is kept in a cell that names it, our reading is in a cell that names it as ours, the writer checks the wording against the verified bytes, and who made the reading is recorded. Do not build a second mechanism for numbers.
7. **One check, registered in `governance/check-registry.yaml`:** `scripts/audit/translation_pointer_audit.py`. For every current translation: the pointer resolves, the hash matches the cell today, the number rule of item 5 holds. It prints `EXAMINED: <n>`. What reaches the guidebook without it: a translation shown beside a quotation it no longer translates, because SQLite cannot hold a foreign key to "any cell". Declare it as the registry declares a check over a table that is empty by decision today (read two existing floorless entries and follow them). The captured set is derived from the writers: confirm `translations` enters it with `dbcore.writable_tables`.
**What reads what this task adds or changes:** `v_translations_current`: the synthesis discussion (T-032), the candidate finder (T-033), render (T-037), and a session comparing forms across languages (T-026, T-107). `translations --due-at`: `/run-pipeline` at each stage. ## Convention 2026-11-12 — how a delegated resolution's standing is recorded, and when it opens a task's gate

Recorded by an Opus-class model in the same delegated pass, after the independent review of condition (d) (`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS-REVIEW.md`) found that every task gate read only the literal `OD-NN:` and so opened on a delegated line before its check was recorded. **This is a convention for reading the ledger, not an owner ruling**; it changes no ruling and no doctrine, and the owner may replace it.

**Two kinds of line, latest wins.** For each decision of the register `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` §8, the ledger carries:
- a status line, `OD-NN STATUS: <value>`, one of: `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER` (written by the session that records the owner's quoted answer), `RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION`, `WITHDRAWN, REFERRED BACK TO THE OWNER`, `REFERRED BACK TO THE OWNER`;
- for a delegated resolution, a check line, `OD-NN CHECK: <value>`, one of: `not required`, `pending`, `confirmed`, `confirmed with corrections applied`, `referred back`.

Each is read as the last line of its kind for that id: `grep -F "OD-NN STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1`, and the same for `CHECK:`. A later line supersedes an earlier one; no line is edited.

**The gate.** A task's precondition on a decision is OPEN only when (1) the last status line is `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`, or (2) the last status line is `RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION` **and** the last check line is `not required`, `confirmed` or `confirmed with corrections applied`. Every other state is CLOSED, including no status line at all, `pending`, a withdrawn resolution and a referral. **A task whose text requires the owner's own words** (for example the mobility split, T-102) **is open only on `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`**; a delegated resolution never satisfies it. The one command a task file uses:

```
gate(){ s=$(grep -F "$1 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); c=$(grep -F "$1 CHECK:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); case "$s" in *"ANSWERED BY THE OWNER"*) echo "$1 OPEN (owner)";; *"RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION"*) case "$c" in *"not required"*|*confirmed*) echo "$1 OPEN (delegated; ${c#*CHECK: })";; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (check: ${c:-none})";; esac;; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (${s:-no status line})";; esac; }
```

**What it replaces.** The `grep -n -F "OD-NN:"` checks in the task files, which a delegated line, a withdrawn line and an owner's answer all satisfied alike. The `OD-NN:` answer lines stay as the record of what was answered; they no longer open a gate by themselves.

CONDITION: any task or session deciding whether a register decision is settled enough to act on.
ACTION: (1) Run the gate above for each decision the task names; act only on OPEN. (2) For a task that requires the owner's words, act only on `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`. (3) When recording an owner's answer to a register decision, add the line `OD-NN STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER` in the same entry. (4) Never edit a status or check line; append a new one.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — convention recorded in the delegated pass, not an owner statement.


## Correction 2026-11-12 — to the delegated resolution of OD-14, the rows written under MOB: withdrawn and referred back to the owner

A correction by the Opus-class model that wrote the delegated resolution "Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-14 carrying the rows written under MOB since the split was ratified" above, on the independent review of condition (d). **That resolution is withdrawn.** It is not the owner's words and never was; nothing may be built on it.

**Why.** Its decisive argument was that the owner's 2026-08-25 ruling ("yes, AMB and WHEEL to fan out") lost its force because its reason was removed by the 2026-08-27 overruling of DR-2026-08-24 §2.4. That reason is the recording session's gloss, not the owner's words; the choice the owner was shown was "fan" or "drop" (`scratchpad/session_2026-08-25-pipeline-smoke-test-mobility/logs/F5-population-split-design.md` §8 item 2), not fan-out against judging; and concluding that an owner rule no longer binds because a later ruling removed its basis, where the later ruling does not name it, is the act the delegation reserved (OD-13 in the register; condition (e)). It also presupposed the answer to an open owner question, GAP-076 (whether a clause that names no one but sits under a disability heading carries `MOB` or `ALL`).

**A narrower version exists, and is left for the owner to take or refuse.** The review found it sound in principle: (1) the 2026-08-25 ruling's operative words cover the 31 `item_population_links` rows of a table since dropped; (2) every figure now under `MOB` was written after the split and after the 2026-08-27 ruling placed the crossing at judgment (`python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute(\"select min(created_at),max(created_at),count(*) from source_value_extractions where identity_code='MOB'\").fetchall())"`); (3) the ruling's grade clause ("Not fanned out, ever") is kept in full; (4) rows whose `MOB` tag rests on a heading and whose text names no group wait on GAP-076 (`select status, description from gaps where gap_id='GAP-076'`); (5) `evidence_population_match` has no retirement column (`PRAGMA table_info(evidence_population_match)`), so retiring grade rows needs a tooling change first, and `base_taxonomy_identity.status` takes `deprecated`, not "retired". **The question for the owner, in one line:** "The 2026-08-25 fan-out ruling covered the 31 item links. For the post-split MOB figures and grades, may judgment tag each row by the users it names, fanning out (flagged) only rows that name neither group; and is a clause that names no one but sits under a disability heading MOB or ALL (GAP-076)?" The wording for part-time wheelchair users is also the owner's.

OD-14 STATUS: WITHDRAWN, REFERRED BACK TO THE OWNER
OD-14 CHECK: referred back

CONDITION: any session executing the mobility split, tagging AMB or WHEEL, re-grading population matches against MOB, or reading the withdrawn OD-14 entry above.
ACTION: (1) Treat the delegated OD-14 resolution as withdrawn; build nothing on it. (2) Start the mobility split (T-102) only when the status line for OD-14 reads ANSWERED BY THE OWNER. (3) Put the one-line question above, with GAP-076, to the owner.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — correction in the delegated pass, not an owner statement.


## Correction 2026-11-12 — to the delegated resolution of OD-01, jurisdiction in a determination

A correction, on the independent review of condition (d), to "Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-01 jurisdiction in a determination, sub-national codes, climate and culture" above. Still a delegated resolution, not the owner's words. The review confirmed it with corrections; these are the corrections, and they are applied.

1. **The parent is a provenance relation only.** The sentence of the resolutions file "Coverage and scope roll up through the parent", and the entry's reversal clause "a scope rule that the roll-up misroutes", are withdrawn. Whether a sub-national instrument counts toward its country's coverage, or owes coverage of its own, is the reserved scope decision (OD-04 in the register). A provincial code must not stand in for its country's coverage: REF-01013 was admitted because the national standard was blocked (`sessions/session_2026-09-28-research-batch-22-selection.md:72`).
2. **Four held cases, not two.** GAP-077 (`select description from gaps where gap_id='GAP-077'`) names REF-00992 (Approved Document M vol. 2, "for use in England", filed `UK`), REF-00995 (Flemish Government decree, filed `BE`), REF-01013 (Ontario Building Code, filed `CA`) and REF-01029 (a Madrid methodology, filed `ES`).
3. **Warrants.** Branching a determination by a climatic or cultural condition rests on OR-2 ("Branches, and an empty headline when all are conditioned"). The Kawa and PAS 6463 rules and `governance/armature_v4_resolutions.md` Q29 (an Opus 4.6 resolution, not an owner ruling) warrant only that culture and climate are conditions, not keys. A cultural condition that branches a figure keeps the Kawa rule's flag for Person Mode co-design ("Specify the physics; flag the spatial model for Person Mode co-design").
4. **Spelling.** A sub-national code follows ISO 3166-2 except where the project convention overrides it: under `UK`, never `GB` (`governance/jurisdiction-philosophy.md` §3.3), so England's code is spelled with the `UK` prefix.

OD-01 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-01 CHECK: confirmed with corrections applied

CONDITION: any session designing the jurisdiction registry, filing a sub-national instrument, or recording a climatic or cultural condition.
ACTION: (1) Give a sub-national instrument its own code with its country as parent, as provenance only; decide nothing about its coverage. (2) Re-file the four held cases in a research pull request after the registry exists. (3) Branch by a climatic or cultural condition under OR-2, and keep the Person Mode co-design flag on a cultural branch. (4) Spell sub-national codes under the UK convention.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — correction in the delegated pass, not an owner statement.


## Correction 2026-11-12 — to the delegated resolution of OD-02, the language of a page

A correction, on the independent review of condition (d), to "Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-02 the language of a page, and how a translated quotation is shown" above. Still a delegated resolution, not the owner's words; confirmed with corrections, which are applied.

1. **It is a reading of the owner's words under condition (c).** The owner's statement of 2026-11-12 asks that the pipeline "render across a multitude of languages and jurisdictions", and its entry records what that means as open and the owner's (`grep -n -F "render across languages" references/project-standards.md`). ## Convention 2026-11-12 — how a delegated resolution's standing is recorded, and when it opens a task's gate

Recorded by an Opus-class model in the same delegated pass, after the independent review of condition (d) (`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS-REVIEW.md`) found that every task gate read only the literal `OD-NN:` and so opened on a delegated line before its check was recorded. **This is a convention for reading the ledger, not an owner ruling**; it changes no ruling and no doctrine, and the owner may replace it.

**Two kinds of line, latest wins.** For each decision of the register `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` §8, the ledger carries:
- a status line, `OD-NN STATUS: <value>`, one of: `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER` (written by the session that records the owner's quoted answer), `RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION`, `WITHDRAWN, REFERRED BACK TO THE OWNER`, `REFERRED BACK TO THE OWNER`;
- for a delegated resolution, a check line, `OD-NN CHECK: <value>`, one of: `not required`, `pending`, `confirmed`, `confirmed with corrections applied`, `referred back`.

Each is read as the last line of its kind for that id: `grep -F "OD-NN STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1`, and the same for `CHECK:`. A later line supersedes an earlier one; no line is edited.

**The gate.** A task's precondition on a decision is OPEN only when (1) the last status line is `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`, or (2) the last status line is `RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION` **and** the last check line is `not required`, `confirmed` or `confirmed with corrections applied`. Every other state is CLOSED, including no status line at all, `pending`, a withdrawn resolution and a referral. **A task whose text requires the owner's own words** (for example the mobility split, T-102) **is open only on `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`**; a delegated resolution never satisfies it. The one command a task file uses:

```
gate(){ s=$(grep -F "$1 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); c=$(grep -F "$1 CHECK:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); case "$s" in *"ANSWERED BY THE OWNER"*) echo "$1 OPEN (owner)";; *"RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION"*) case "$c" in *"not required"*|*confirmed*) echo "$1 OPEN (delegated; ${c#*CHECK: })";; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (check: ${c:-none})";; esac;; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (${s:-no status line})";; esac; }
```

**What it replaces.** The `grep -n -F "OD-NN:"` checks in the task files, which a delegated line, a withdrawn line and an owner's answer all satisfied alike. The `OD-NN:` answer lines stay as the record of what was answered; they no longer open a gate by themselves.

CONDITION: any task or session deciding whether a register decision is settled enough to act on.
ACTION: (1) Run the gate above for each decision the task names; act only on OPEN. (2) For a task that requires the owner's words, act only on `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`. (3) When recording an owner's answer to a register decision, add the line `OD-NN STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER` in the same entry. (4) Never edit a status or check line; append a new one.

import re, sys
from pathlib import Path
T = Path("/home/user/guidebook/workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks")

GATE = ('gate(){ s=$(grep -F "$1 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); c=$(grep -F "$1 CHECK:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); '
        'case "$s" in *"ANSWERED BY THE OWNER"*) echo "$1 OPEN (owner)";; *"RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION"*) case "$c" in *"not required"*|*confirmed*) '
        'echo "$1 OPEN (delegated; ${c#*CHECK: })";; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (check: ${c:-none})";; esac;; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (${s:-no status line})";; esac; }')
CONV = '`grep -n -F "Convention 2026-11-12 — how a delegated resolution" references/project-standards.md`'
OWNER_NONE = "- **Owner decisions:** none outstanding. The decisions this task needed are resolved under delegation (next bullet); none is still the owner's."
STOP = ("- the delegation gate of section 2 prints CLOSED for a decision this task rests on (the owner has reversed it, a correction has withdrawn it, "
        "or its independent check is not recorded); a delegated resolution is never the owner's words;")
ANCHOR9 = "- you would have to guess a value, a vocabulary term, a name or an owner's intent."


def f(tid):
    m = list(T.glob(f"{tid}-*.md"))
    assert len(m) == 1, tid
    return m[0]


def rd(tid):
    return f(tid).read_text()


def wr(tid, t):
    f(tid).write_text(t)


def once(t, old, new, tid):
    n = t.count(old)
    assert n == 1, (tid, n, old[:80])
    return t.replace(old, new)


def deleg(ods, notes):
    return ("- **Delegated resolutions this task rests on.** " + notes +
            " Each is a resolution by an Opus-class model under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-12: not the owner's words, reversible by the owner, "
            f"and read only through the ledger's gate ({CONV}). Run it before you start and again before you open the pull request; if any line prints CLOSED, stop (section 9):\n"
            "```\n" + GATE + "\nfor n in " + " ".join(ods) + "; do gate $n; done\n```")


def set_owner(tid, t, new_owner, delegated=None):
    lines = t.split("\n")
    i = next(k for k, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith("- **Owner decisions"))
    j = i + 1
    while j < len(lines) and lines[j].startswith("  - "):
        j += 1
    block = [new_owner] + ([delegated] if delegated else [])
    lines[i:j] = block
    return "\n".join(lines)


def set_deps(tid, t, deps):
    m = re.search(r"^- \*\*Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:\*\* (.*?) Check by running", t, re.M)
    assert m, tid
    return t[:m.start(1)] + deps + t[m.end(1):]


def set_change(tid, t, items, reads=None):
    m = re.search(r"(Order of preference, from CLAUDE\.md §8:[^\n]*\n\n)(.*?)(\n\n\*\*What reads what this task adds or changes:\*\*)([^\n]*)", t, re.S)
    assert m, tid
    r = m.group(4) if reads is None else " " + reads
    return t[:m.start(2)] + items + m.group(3) + r + t[m.end(4):]


def add_stop(tid, t):
    return once(t, ANCHOR9, ANCHOR9 + "\n" + STOP, tid)


def step2(tid, t, old_prefix, new):
    m = re.search(r"^" + re.escape(old_prefix) + r".*$", t, re.M)
    assert m, tid
    return t[:m.start()] + new + t[m.end():]


def names(tid, t, extra):
    m = re.search(r"^Names to sweep: (.*)$", t, re.M)
    assert m, tid
    return t[:m.end()] + ", " + extra + t[m.end():]


def delegated_task(tid, ods, notes, deps=None, items=None, reads=None, s2=None, extra_names=None):
    t = rd(tid)
    if deps:
        t = set_deps(tid, t, deps)
    t = set_owner(tid, t, OWNER_NONE, deleg(ods, notes))
    if items is not None:
        t = set_change(tid, t, items, reads)
    if s2:
        t = step2(tid, t, s2[0], s2[1])
    if extra_names:
        t = names(tid, t, extra_names)
    t = add_stop(tid, t)
    wr(tid, t)


# ---------- T-019 (OD-08)
t = rd("T-019")
delegated_task("T-019", ["OD-08"],
    "OD-08: an absent cell has no row — a lens that is relevant to the parameter but carried by no figure gets no determination row; the absence is recorded as an open gap by the judgment session that judges the lens relevant (with `add-gap` and the parameter and lens columns of T-013), never by the engine.",
    items=None)
t = rd("T-019")
t = once(t, "3. The rule label is bumped as the workplan says (WR-2); it is not an open question.",
         "3. The rule label is bumped as the workplan says (WR-2); it is not an open question.\n"
         "4. **The absent-cell sub-case (OD-08, resolved under delegation: no row).** The engine writes no determination row for a lens no figure of the parameter carries, "
         "whether or not anyone judges that lens relevant: relevance without a figure is a gap, raised at judgment through `add-gap`, not a `pending` row. "

            "```\n" + GATE + "\nfor n in " + " ".join(ods) + "; do gate $n; done\n```")


def set_owner(tid, t, new_owner, delegated=None):
    lines = t.split("\n")
    i = next(k for k, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith("- **Owner decisions"))
    j = i + 1
    while j < len(lines) and lines[j].startswith("  - "):
        j += 1
    block = [new_owner] + ([delegated] if delegated else [])
    lines[i:j] = block
    return "\n".join(lines)


def set_deps(tid, t, deps):
    m = re.search(r"^- \*\*Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:\*\* (.*?) Check by running", t, re.M)
    assert m, tid
    return t[:m.start(1)] + deps + t[m.end(1):]


def set_change(tid, t, items, reads=None):
    m = re.search(r"(Order of preference, from CLAUDE\.md §8:[^\n]*\n\n)(.*?)(\n\n\*\*What reads what this task adds or changes:\*\*)([^\n]*)", t, re.S)
    assert m, tid
    r = m.group(4) if reads is None else " " + reads
    return t[:m.start(2)] + items + m.group(3) + r + t[m.end(4):]


def add_stop(tid, t):
    return once(t, ANCHOR9, ANCHOR9 + "\n" + STOP, tid)


def step2(tid, t, old_prefix, new):
    m = re.search(r"^" + re.escape(old_prefix) + r".*$", t, re.M)
    assert m, tid
    return t[:m.start()] + new + t[m.end():]


def names(tid, t, extra):
    m = re.search(r"^Names to sweep: (.*)$", t, re.M)
    assert m, tid
    return t[:m.end()] + ", " + extra + t[m.end():]


def delegated_task(tid, ods, notes, deps=None, items=None, reads=None, s2=None, extra_names=None):
    t = rd(tid)
    if deps:
        t = set_deps(tid, t, deps)
    t = set_owner(tid, t, OWNER_NONE, deleg(ods, notes))
    if items is not None:
        t = set_change(tid, t, items, reads)
    if s2:
        t = step2(tid, t, s2[0], s2[1])
    if extra_names:
        t = names(tid, t, extra_names)
    t = add_stop(tid, t)
    wr(tid, t)
